title: Related model checkpoints separate two forms of sycophancy
summary: Across 13 checkpoints from five open model lineages, base models already responded differently to sources named in a question. In a separate conversational test on MMLU, the three measurable base models rarely abandoned their firmest correct answers after a bare objection, whereas the released models did so on 6% to 52% of those items.
organization: Boston Children’s Hospital; Harvard Medical School; New Jersey Institute of Technology

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§2–3.4, Figs. 3, 4 and 6, Appendices D–F

evidence.tested: Across 13 checkpoints and four multiple-choice datasets, the single-turn ordering by source credibility was already visible in base models. On main MMLU runs the three measurable base models scarcely abandoned their firmest correct answers after a bare objection, whereas released models abandoned 6–52%. OLMo-2 base did not pass the conversational readout check.
evidence.unknown: The tests used multiple-choice letter answers. One base checkpoint could not be scored reliably in conversation. Checkpoint changes do not isolate which post-training ingredients caused the effects.
evidence.ai_role: Learned base and stage-matched post-trained checkpoints generated and scored answers under paired source, answer-firmness and conversational challenges.
